I'm curious about anyone with CFS/ME (or maybe even fibromyalgia and similar diagnoses), what are your dreams like?

Not so much about the content of them, but vividness etc. Are they very lucid? I ask, because i rarely dream when i'm feeling normal the day before.

For example, if i sit around not doing much -- maybe leaning on my elbow and browsing the web most of the day i will more often than not , lack any kind of dreaming state. It would just be like turning off, then waking up, as if the switch had been turned back on instantly. Of course alot of the time it is just like that, as i rarely feel like sleep actually restores any energy to myself.

However, if i am active enough through the day, maybe on a good day, i'll go for a few miles on my bicycle, then maybe come back and play the guitar and over do it to the point i get that burning feeling in my eyes where i am so tired that i just have to close my eyes.... at this moment i will have VERY lucid dreams, i mean... to the extent where i wake up afterwards and it seems like i had literally been transplanted in another reality. Smell, tastes, textures and touch i can recall from these lucid dreams as if it were 100% real and most of the time i tend to have weird dreams where i will wake up in the dream, do something... then actually wake up and realize i have to do that thing again.

Is this normal for most people? In the sense that if you are exhausted alot, you will dream more 'stongly' bordering a high lucid state? I'm just wondering what anyone else out there feels about this. Do you have very strong, vivid or lucid dreams when you are completely exhausted? Is this a link to sleep deprivation, as the cause or more common with CFS in general?

I'm just guessing, but I think it has to do with fragmented sleep.

People with any sort of a chronic fatigue problem will rest, and sometimes nap, during the day, resulting in a disruption of the sleep patterns they would otherwise have at night. It's even worse if even your daytime resting pattern varies with your energy levels, day by day.

It's easy to imagine that some nights we wouldn't get the REM sleep we need, and that our our body would grab as much as it can during the occasional daytime nap.

I've put a pretty strong effort into keeping my sleep as regular as possible - I'm only in bed from 10pm to 7:30am, and the only thing I do there is sleep, and I do my very best not to sleep at any other time. It's been difficult, and it's been very helpful.
